question: A company aims to optimize project team compositions by forming a specialized 'Innovation Hub' combining employees from its Engineering (200 employees) and Marketing (100 employees) departments. Given that the average monthly salary for the Engineering department is $6000 and for Marketing is $4500, if the target average monthly salary for the Innovation Hub is $5500, the required ratio of employees from Engineering to Marketing is ____. Concurrently, if the average years of experience for Engineering is 8 years and for Marketing is 6 years, and the desired average experience for the Innovation Hub is 7.5 years, the ratio of employees from Engineering to Marketing based on experience targets would be ____. Based on the departmental employee counts and these derived ratios, the maximum number of employees that can be drawn to form this 'Innovation Hub' while adhering strictly to *both* the salary and experience target average profiles simultaneously, is ____. This constraint highlights a significant ____ in optimizing combined team profiles, necessitating a sophisticated HR approach to reconcile competing metrics and ensure overall organizational ____.
title: Mixture & Alligation: HR Departmental Average Salary & Experience Analysis
solution: "The company decides to form a new 'Special Projects Division' by transferring 60% of the employees from the Engineering department and 40% of the employees from the Sales department. To further boost its capabilities, the company plans to hire additional data analysts for this division. Each new data analyst has an average monthly salary of $6,000 and an average experience of 6 years. If, after these new hires, the overall average monthly salary of the 'Special Projects Division' becomes $7,000, what is the number of new data analysts hired? Also, what would be the overall average years of experience of the 'Special Projects Division' after these new hires?"
